### EXT-152 — Current funding routes separate company R&D, public research, and individual support

**Finding.** As of 2026-07-24, several current programs are relevant to an
early robot-policy-evaluation venture, but they fund materially different
applicants and outputs:

- NIST's active 2025-NIST-MSE-01 notice accepts for-profit organizations,
  requires no cost share, and closes September 15, 2026. Its Engineering
  Laboratory scope explicitly includes measurement methods for integrating,
  testing, and validating digital twins and performance metrics, test
  artifacts, reference data, and software for robotic and autonomous systems.
  The notice states an EL award range of $5,000–$500,000 per year with periods
  up to five years, but the EL amount is labeled FY 2024 and all awards and
  continuations depend on program needs and available funds. A fit-and-funding
  inquiry is therefore required before a full application is treated as a
  live opportunity. The notice also states that applications for product
  development or commercialization are nonresponsive. NIST is therefore a
  ring-fenced measurement-science route, not direct company-product funding.
- NSF 26-510 is an active U.S. small-business R&D route. Phase I provides up
  to $305,000 for 6–18 months; a Project Pitch and invitation are required;
  the next practical full-proposal deadlines are November 4, 2026, March 4,
  2027, and July 7, 2027. The PI does not need a degree or academic
  affiliation, but must have the legal right to work for the U.S. company and
  be at least 51% employed by it during the award.
- NSF 26-512, posted July 21, 2026, accepts U.S.-based for-profit
  organizations and has a November 4, 2026 deadline. It anticipates planning
  grants up to $200,000, Impact awards up to $2 million, and Flagship awards
  up to $5 million. Its scope is AI enablement, augmentation, harmonization,
  governance, and availability of **existing** scientific datasets; de novo
  data collection is out of scope.
- Activate's U.S. Cohort 2027 applications are scheduled to open September
  15, 2026. Its fellowship provides more than $300,000 over two years, takes
  no equity, names robotics/AI/control-related verticals, and expects the
  funded principal applicant to work full-time on the company. The current
  eligibility page also requires the principal to be a first-time commercial
  leader of a hardware-based technology innovation and to have a bachelor's
  degree plus at least four years of post-baccalaureate technical experience.
  Its FAQ documents some pure-software exceptions, so Auspex requires a
  program fit check rather than being treated as clearly eligible.
- Emergent Ventures currently accepts applications from entrepreneurs and
  researchers worldwide but publishes no standard award amount on its program
  page. Manifund lets anyone publish a proposal in science and technology but
  limits grants to legally qualifying public-benefit work under a grant
  agreement.
- Anthropic Fellows is an individual four-month full-time empirical-AI
  research program, not company financing; its current November cohort closes
  July 26, 2026 and lists a $3,850 weekly U.S. stipend and approximately
  $15,000 per month of compute. NIST currently lists research-associate
  openings in AI/autonomous/HRI evaluation; associates receive salary and
  benefits through a partner university or contractor. These are personal
  research/employment pathways, not capital for Auspex.
- Astera does not currently show an open residency application. Its current
  open-science policy says work and IP created during employment or contract
  are Astera-owned and research outputs are to be openly published. It is a
  watchlist route for a ring-fenced public project, not a safe source for
  proprietary Auspex work without a written pre-award carveout.
- Robotics Factory's 2026 application deadline passed on July 18, 2026 and
  its up-to-$100,000 convertible note requires a significant Southwestern
  Pennsylvania presence for the program and five years afterward. The official
  MassRobotics Accelerator page describes completed 2024 and 2025 cohorts,
  not a current open cash program.
- MassRobotics' 2026 IROS Pitchfest closes August 20, 2026 and offers first-
  and second-place cash prizes of $10,000 and $5,000. It requires an
  incorporated company less than five years old, fewer than 20 staff, and less
  than $2 million in venture funding. This is a small prize rather than
  research financing.

### EXT-153 — Historical recipient profiles favor bounded technical risk, physical evidence, and directly relevant execution

**Finding.** A purposefully matched sample of official recipient and award
histories changes the relative funding assessment for Auspex:

- NSF SBIR is the strongest company-building analogue. Robotics and adjacent
  recipients describe a specific high-risk technical innovation, measurable
  prototype objectives, a concrete initial market, and directly relevant team
  capability. Openspace's Phase I award 1721381 funded fast creation of
  photorealistic site models from consumer hardware and named model-quality,
  on-device, and route-generation hurdles. Diligent Droids' Phase I award
  1621651 linked a service-robot learning program to a hospital partner and
  deployment evidence. RightHand Robotics and more recent Phase I recipients
  likewise present bounded technical milestones and an integrated physical
  prototype path. Existing revenue and a Ph.D. are not universal requirements,
  but an eligible incorporated small business is required for a full
  application.
- Activate is materially more plausible than a literal “hardware manufacturer”
  reading implies. Activate recipient Reforge Robotics uses software and
  computation to improve force control and accuracy in lower-cost commercial
  robots. rStream also couples robotics software and engineering with a
  physical waste-sorting system. Activate's own FAQ says pure-software
  innovations may fit when scientific de-risking, hardware integration,
  unusual capital requirements, unclear applications, or exceptional impact
  apply. Incorporation is not required and provides no application advantage.
  Most applicants nevertheless have experimental proof-of-concept data, and
  applicants must articulate credible IP-compatible access to the tools,
  equipment, facilities, and collaborators required by the fellowship start.
- NIST MSE is an unusually close topic match but a weaker startup-financing
  route. Carnegie Mellon award 70NANB24H314 addressed validation and deployment
  of AI-powered manufacturing robots through standardized metrics, generative
  simulation over environmental and physical variations, and failure
  analysis. Other purpose-matched recent awards cover robot anomaly-data
  quality, stability and grasping test methods, synthetic/real benchmarks,
  task-representation standards, and embodied-AI reference platforms.
  For-profit recipients exist, but matched company awards concern
  vendor-neutral guides, standards, or test methods. The current solicitation
  explicitly makes product-development and commercialization applications
  nonresponsive. Public recipient lists are institution-heavy: FY2024 and
  FY2025 Information Technology Laboratory lists contain institutional
  recipients, while the older FY2013 Engineering Laboratory list contains 21
  awards and one named LLC. The ITL lists are not a direct EL comparator and
  are used only as directional evidence.
- The sole directly comparable MassRobotics ICRA Pitch Competition winner
  publicly identified for 2025, ReviMo, was an incorporated physical-product
  company with a demonstrable personal robotic assistant. This single,
  ecosystem-connected winner cannot establish a general selection mechanism,
  but it does show a substantially higher demonstration and company-readiness
  level than Auspex currently has.
- Anthropic publishes project outputs rather than a complete historical
  credential distribution. It reports that more than 80% of its first cohort
  produced papers and more than 40% subsequently joined Anthropic. Its examples
  are empirical AI-safety studies and open tools shaped with mentors. The
  `ppi-gold-bias` scalable-oversight work, not Auspex's robotics-company
  maturity, is the relevant basis for the already submitted application.
- NSF 26-512 was posted on 2026-07-21 and has no historical cohort under that
  exact solicitation. No “winner profile” is inferred for the program.

The common competitive profile is a founder or team with directly relevant
execution evidence, one sharply defined technical uncertainty, and a credible
path to physical or empirical validation. For Auspex, the most reusable missing
artifact is a minimal capture-to-twin-to-prediction experiment with controlled
simulated variation, a small matched real-robot trial set, and a demonstrated
advance/test-more/abstain decision. That would improve Activate and NSF SBIR
readiness and support a separately ring-fenced NIST research inquiry. It does
not require Auspex to manufacture a robot.

**Status.** confirmed at the cited recipient/project scope; the inference about
selection patterns remains qualified

**Evidence basis.** source-verified; independent challenge completed

### EXT-154 — Runpod local Pod volumes are machine-bound, and tested `/workspace` mode semantics differed from container-local storage

**Finding.** Runpod's current Pod-migration documentation states that a Pod is
tied to a particular physical machine. Stopping the Pod releases its GPU; if
that GPU is occupied later, the stopped Pod cannot simply resume elsewhere
without migration. Runpod's storage documentation distinguishes the default
local volume disk, retained with the Pod until deletion, from a portable
network volume that exists independently and can attach across Pods.

This documented boundary explains why the stopped first attempt-08 builder
could retain its data yet fail to restart when the original machine's A40 was
unavailable. It does not imply that no A40 existed elsewhere. For expensive
builds that must survive machine loss, a content-identified off-host archive
or network volume is required; stopping a local-volume Pod alone is not a
portable environment artifact.

A separate provider observation is narrower. On disposable secure-A40 canary
pod `wmxuozguiu1isl`, extracting the portable harness archive into
`/workspace` changed archived modes 0644/0755 to observed 0666/0777 while
preserving file hashes. Extracting the same archive into container-local
`/opt` preserved root ownership, exact 0644/0755 modes, executable status, and
all four hashes. The scientific runtime therefore used `/opt` for the
executable harness and retained `/workspace` for inputs and outputs.

Runpod's cited documentation does not state this mode-normalization behavior.
It is recorded only as a reproduced property of the tested Pod/storage path,
not as a platform-wide guarantee or filesystem diagnosis.

**Status.** confirmed at the cited documentation and tested secure-A40 Pod
scope; mode behavior is provider-observed, not generalized

**Evidence basis.** official documentation plus independently retained
provider canary evidence

**Evidence and trace.**

- Runpod, “Pod migration,”
  <https://docs.runpod.io/pods/troubleshooting/pod-migration>, retrieved
  2026-07-24. The page states the physical-machine binding, GPU release on
  stop, restart/migration consequence, and network-volume alternative.
- Runpod, “Storage options,”
  <https://docs.runpod.io/pods/storage/types>, retrieved 2026-07-24. The page
  distinguishes local volume disks from independently retained, portable
  network volumes.
- Attempt-08 canary failure trace:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/work/oscar-input-reconstruction/attempt08-operator/canary-failure-network-mode-normalization/`.
- Passed container-local canary archive SHA-256
  `6ab6ad56534a4d4c0e1f723be916a1159db97b312269b16f44ed9482903aef65`,
  under
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/work/oscar-input-reconstruction/attempt08-operator/canary-pass-container-local-v3/`.
- Attempt-08 operator record:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/work/oscar-input-reconstruction/attempt08-operator/operator-record.md`.

**Uncertainty and remaining validation.** The exact `/workspace` backing
filesystem and the layer responsible for mode normalization were not
identified. Other data centers, Pod images, local volumes, network volumes,
mount options, or provider revisions may behave differently. Revalidate
archive metadata on the target path whenever ownership or executable bits are
load-bearing.

**Status history.**

- 2026-07-24 — Created as `confirmed at the cited documentation and tested
  secure-A40 Pod scope; mode behavior is provider-observed, not generalized`
  after official documentation review, observed local-volume restart refusal,
  a same-image canary reproducing `/workspace` mode normalization, and a
  same-canary `/opt` extraction passing exact metadata and hash checks.

### EXT-155 — OSCAR pins its processor revision but not the text-encoder weight lookup

**Finding.** At OSCAR source commit
`4dea2f657e221b0ff24c895fcc8ab4d46d5a9adb`, the public checkpoint registry
maps the Qwen processor's internal S3-style URI to
`nvidia/Cosmos-Reason1-7B` revision
`3210bec0495fdc7a8d3dbb8d58da5711eab4b423`. The runtime therefore logs and
downloads that pinned revision while constructing the processor.

The actual text-encoder weight path follows a different branch. The OSCAR
experiment configuration defaults `ckpt_path` to the bare repository ID
`nvidia/Cosmos-Reason1-7B`. Public `get_checkpoint_path()` treats a
repo-ID-shaped string as a Hugging Face reference and calls
`snapshot_download(repo_id=checkpoint_uri)` without a `revision`. The text
encoder is therefore resolved at the repository head unless the operator
supplies `COSMOS_REASON_PATH`.

The retained Attempt-08 runtime loaded the text encoder from snapshot
`375e24000b24baed78f4618d3dd779e47cd96323`, not from the processor's pinned
`3210bec...` snapshot. The official Hugging Face API reports `375e240...` as
the current head, last modified 2025-12-10. A file-level API comparison between
the two revisions found identical blob IDs and LFS SHA-256 values for every
model shard, configuration, tokenizer, processor, and template file; only
`README.md` changed. Thus the unversioned resolution did not change the
scientific auxiliary weights or configuration in the retained Attempt-08 run,
but the released environment contract remains open to future head drift.

Attempt 09 independently traversed the same two source paths in both baseline
processes and loaded the same `375e240...` text-encoder snapshot. Before the
pod was stopped, all 13 resolved snapshot files, including four model shards,
were hashed and byte-counted; the selecting source files and runtime log
excerpts were retained in an archive bound to the science-session hash. This
closes the exact auxiliary contents used in Attempt 09 but does not close the
released default against a future repository-head change.

**Status.** confirmed at the pinned source, retained Attempt-08 runtime, and
cited Hugging Face revision scope

**Evidence basis.** source-verified, provider-observed, and file-inventory
reproduced

**Evidence and trace.**

- Official OSCAR repository,
  <https://github.com/wuzy2115/oscar-public>, commit
  `4dea2f657e221b0ff24c895fcc8ab4d46d5a9adb`, retrieved 2026-07-25:
  - `worldsim/_ext/imaginaire/utils/checkpoint_db.py`, especially the Qwen
    processor registry entry with revision `3210bec...` and
    `get_checkpoint_path()`'s bare-repository branch;
  - `worldsim/_src/configs/agibot_control/experiment/cosmos2/v2_with_human_70f.py`,
    where `COSMOS_REASON_PATH` defaults to the unversioned repository ID; and
  - `worldsim/_src/predict2/text_encoders/text_encoder.py`, where the configured
    path is passed to `get_checkpoint_path()` before weights are loaded.
- Retained Attempt-08 runtime log:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/work/oscar-input-reconstruction/attempt08-operator/science-session-v3/oscar-layerwise-session-attempt08/logs/baseline-repeat-a.log`.
  It records the processor request at `3210bec...` and the text-encoder load
  from cache snapshot `375e240...`.
- Attempt-09 auxiliary evidence archive SHA-256
  `81cba27f6b8634e5bcbb89e793185252d8a502258ac0afc2352879a46333bb87`,
  under
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/oscar-input-reconstruction/runs/attempt09-auxiliary-evidence.tar.gz`.
  Its verified manifest contains the source-path and two runtime-log excerpts,
  and its snapshot tables contain SHA-256 values and byte counts for all 13
  resolved files. The archive binds itself to science-session SHA-256
  `406d5621029c793c2e9754be125e9bed638959cc54927f2c1ee1bdde646ba1da`.
- Official Hugging Face model APIs for
  `nvidia/Cosmos-Reason1-7B` at revisions
  `3210bec0495fdc7a8d3dbb8d58da5711eab4b423` and
  `375e24000b24baed78f4618d3dd779e47cd96323`, queried with
  `blobs=true` on 2026-07-25. The comparison sorted each sibling by filename,
  blob ID, LFS SHA-256, and byte count; the only difference was `README.md`.

**Uncertainty and remaining validation.** This comparison establishes content
identity only between the two cited revisions. A later Hugging Face head may
change weights, tokenizer/configuration, or custom files. The fixed scientific
environment should therefore include the resolved auxiliary snapshot and its
file manifest, or set `COSMOS_REASON_PATH` to a locally verified immutable
copy. This finding does not identify the source of OSCAR's same-seed
nondeterminism because both retained Attempt-08 repeats used the same resolved
snapshot.

**Status history.**

- 2026-07-25 — Created as `confirmed at the pinned source, retained Attempt-08
  runtime, and cited Hugging Face revision scope` after source-path tracing,
  retained-log verification, and a full Hugging Face sibling/blob comparison.
  This narrows the earlier broad statement that the auxiliary
  Cosmos-Reason1 dependency was pinned: the processor is pinned, while the
  actual text-encoder weight lookup is not.
- 2026-07-25 — Retained the same status after Attempt 09 reproduced both
  source branches in two more baseline processes, loaded the same
  `375e240...` snapshot, and preserved a verified 13-file snapshot manifest.
  The new evidence closes the exact Attempt-09 auxiliary bytes; it does not
  change the forward-drift limitation of the unversioned source lookup.

### EXT-156 — OSCAR's fixed Attempt-09 five-step diagnostic repeats exactly; the earlier 35-step contrast is cross-regime

**Finding.** At OSCAR source commit
`4dea2f657e221b0ff24c895fcc8ab4d46d5a9adb`, OSCAR-2B revision
`c9781ffa7dd8556d862d7d9f338a2ea008a58ca6`, and the retained secure-A40
container/runtime, two separate Attempt-09 processes executed the same
five-step `droid_TRI` diagnostic with seed 44. Both exited zero. Their 152
trace records were exactly equal: decoded inputs, token IDs, text embeddings,
three VAE encodes, CPU/device initial noise, six Karras scheduler-step
latents, 12 denoiser calls with 96 retained condition rows, final latent,
decoded float/uint8 output, encoded MP4, and decoded encoded RGB. The gate
recorded zero differing records and no first divergence.

The frozen protocol runs determinism interventions only when the baseline
repeats differ. It therefore correctly skipped post-load cuDNN restoration,
strict deterministic-algorithm/cuBLAS, and math-SDPA arms. No intervention
effect or nondeterminism mechanism is identified.

This result does not supersede EXT-143. The earlier 35-step public-interface
processes differed in every decoded frame, but they used driver `580.159.04`,
host CUDA 13.0, a different A40 UUID, and no retained exact image digest.
Attempt 09 used driver `570.211.01`, CUDA 12.8, a different A40 UUID, and an
exact retained image digest. Step count, input path, instrumentation, driver,
GPU instance, and possibly image identity are co-confounded. The two
observations are individually valid; their contrast is descriptive and does
not identify a workload/path mechanism.

The first Attempt-09 science invocation supplied a checkpoint leaf where the
runner required its parent. It failed closed on `model/model` before model
loading and produced no scientific output. The same pod was corrected only at
the invocation boundary, passed a fresh full readiness gate, and then ran the
successful sealed session. This operator failure is retained separately and
is not counted as a model result.

**Status.** confirmed for the fixed Attempt-09 execution contract; the
earlier smoke remains separately confirmed, while the cross-regime
discriminator and mechanism are unresolved

**Evidence basis.** independently executed, layerwise traced, archive-verified,
and source/artifact/runtime identity checked

### EXT-157 — E2's sparse-pair point-method grid confirms the support tradeoff but exposes numerical and DGP qualification gaps

**Finding.** The frozen E2 point-identification grid generated 2,100 synthetic
datasets: seven scenarios, 500/1,356/2,244 sessions, and 100 outer datasets per
cell. It read no historical or future RoboArena outcomes.

M0 requires all 168 stratum×pair cells. It was reportable in 0/100 datasets in
every 500-session scenario. At 1,356 sessions it was reportable in 91–97% of
uniform-assignment datasets but only 55% under a fixed 3:1 pair-assignment
imbalance. At 2,244 sessions it was reportable in 100% of the six uniform
scenarios and 97% under imbalance. This independently confirms the exact
occupancy result: the existing 500-session zero-reportable smoke is a design
consequence, while a uniform-assignment threshold cannot be transported to an
imbalanced assignment mechanism.

A separate support correction preserves the 1,356-session 95% point-support
threshold but relabels 2,244 as a continuous-uniform optimistic lower bound
for 200 failure-free ordinary bootstrap refits. Because 2,244 is not divisible
by 168, that empirical distribution is unattainable. Exact grouped
inclusion-exclusion gives 94.5007% at 2,244, 94.9962% at 2,263, and the first
attainable maximally balanced threshold at 2,264 with 95.0224%.

The inherited finite-difference BFGS implementation initially reported only
0–17% M1/M2 reportability and frequently fell to zero as sample size grew.
An analytic-gradient correction was fixed before a second output and passed
interior derivative/known-answer checks. Independent challenge then showed
that its absolute-gradient acceptance rule is not sample-scale invariant:
acceptance changes when identical counts are multiplied, when policy labels
are permuted, and when the same full grid runs on Linux rather than macOS.
It also accepts all-tie and Davidson complete-separation infinite-boundary
solutions. The previously reported 61–91%/59–91% M1/M2 reportability rates
and their conditional zero-disagreement result are superseded diagnostics,
not scientific operating characteristics. This is numerical evidence, not
evidence against transitivity.

M3 and M4 always returned a point/bound result. At 500 sessions, M4's mean
maximum value-bound width was about 0.080–0.085 in the six uniform scenarios
and 0.137 under imbalance. At 1,356 sessions it was about 0.0005–0.0016 under
uniform assignment and 0.0096 under imbalance. At 2,244 it was zero in six
scenarios and 0.00054 under imbalance.

M0 and M3 disagreed only in 1% of favorable datasets at 1,356 and 2,244
sessions. The recorded M1/M2 zero-disagreement result is additionally
conditioned on a numerically unstable accepted subset. Neither is robustness
proof. Enrollment and target stratum weights are equal in the generator,
leaving M3's target change largely inactive, and the intransitive cycle
affects policies 2–4 rather than the leading 0–1 decision. The grid therefore
does not discriminate the assumptions it was intended to compare.

M4's unsupported-pair bounds also do not include sampling uncertainty. Even
with zero identification width at 2,244 sessions, its point/bound rule declared
the five-point decision in 16% of the adverse-0.075 datasets. This establishes
that sampling uncertainty must be added around the identification bounds; it
is not a coverage or false-pass estimate for a final procedure.

**Status.** confirmed for M0 support, M4 width, and the
non-discriminating-DGP diagnosis; M1/M2 qualification, reportability, exact
regeneration, and conditional disagreement are superseded and provisional

**Evidence basis.** prospectively fixed simulation, preserved correction
history, M0/M4 cross-platform equivalence, and independent numerical,
boundary, scale, permutation, and provenance challenge

**Evidence and trace.**

- Point-comparison protocol:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/prospective-study-design/protocol-e2-point-method-comparison.md`.
- Legacy numerical-failure result:
  `result-e2-point-method-comparison.json`, content SHA-256
  `543e8040c41f0fbfc77888cd2ae9032500d8e37068ab526a0985bcca30e7ea24`.
- Numerical correction protocol:
  `protocol-e2-structured-optimizer-qualification.md`.
- Qualified result:
  `result-e2-point-method-comparison-qualified.json`, content SHA-256
  `5156d52eb9f011ca96ad31274aceafca2a3226db6e0730890414fa627d60253c`.
- Review:
  `review-e2-point-method-comparison.md`.
- Seven initial focused optimizer tests passed on macOS, but they did not
  exercise count scaling, label-permutation acceptance, all-tie/separation
  boundaries, or another operating system. A full Linux regeneration changed
  M1 reportability in 19/21 cells and M2 in 17/21, by up to 10 and 11
  percentage points; M0/M3 decisions were unchanged within negligible
  roundoff and M4 was exactly identical.

**Uncertainty and remaining validation.** No method in this grid carries
sampling uncertainty for the random evaluator-selected set. The next DGP must
activate unequal enrollment/target weights with policy×site crossover,
top-policy intransitivity, pair-specific tie thresholds, decisive
low-probability edges, and near separation. The subsequent common-grid
comparison must evaluate ordinary, cell-conditioned, and multiplier M0;
a new sample-scale-invariant, permutation-invariant, log-domain,
boundary-aware M1/M2 implementation; M4 sampling bounds; and M3 as a
changed-target sensitivity. Actual assignment probabilities and target
weights, adequate Monte Carlo precision, and cross-platform qualification
remain required before sample-size or method selection.

**Status history.**

### EXT-161 — OSCAR non-repeatability spans all four crossed cells, while default FFmpeg RGB conversion is not portable

**Finding.** In one fixed secure-A40 environment and one prospectively fixed,
time-symmetric execution sequence, all four OSCAR same-seed repeat pairs
differed: requested 5 and 35 steps crossed with the unmodified public CLI and
the instrumented diagnostic surface. All eight processes exited zero without
automatic retry. Every within-cell pair differed in encoded MP4, native
YUV420p, and target-x86 decoded RGB. Both diagnostic pairs had exact decoded
inputs and first differed at the first retained VAE-encode output. Thus,
neither 35 requested steps nor the uninstrumented public surface was necessary
for pairwise non-repeatability in this session, and divergence was present by
the retained VAE-output boundary.

This does not estimate a failure probability, identify the VAE kernel or CUDA
operation responsible, remove process-history or execution-order
explanations, or generalize across seeds, cases, models, hardware, drivers, or
the authors' environment. The earlier equal five-step Attempt-09 pair and
this unequal factorial are jointly evidence of session- or state-sensitive
repeatability, not a contradiction.

A post-outcome decoder audit exposed a distinct reproducibility issue. Native
YUV420p hashes and the complete eight-output equality partition were
byte-identical on Debian 12 amd64 FFmpeg 5.1.9, Debian 12 arm64 FFmpeg 5.1.9,
and macOS arm64 FFmpeg 8.1.2. Default RGB hashes differed among all three
paths. Debian-amd64 FFmpeg 5.1.9 nevertheless reproduced all eight target-x86
FFmpeg 6.1.1 default RGB hashes. The explicitly specified conversion
`scale=640:480:in_color_matrix=bt601:in_range=limited:out_range=full:flags=accurate_rnd+bitexact`
produced byte-identical RGB for all eight outputs on all three independently
executed paths.

The streams are H.264 High, YUV420p, 640×480, 81 frames at 14 fps, and do not
declare color range, matrix, transfer, or primaries. FFmpeg documents
libswscale as its pixel-format conversion library, exposes distinct x86 and
AArch64 backends, and defines `accurate_rnd` and `bitexact` as accurate
rounding and bitexact-output flags. The observed default-RGB difference is
therefore attributed only to the tested decoder build/platform paths; version,
build, backend, and architecture remain co-confounded. BT.601 limited-range
is an explicit reproducibility convention, not proof of uniquely intended
colorimetry.

**Status.** confirmed for the fixed factorial environment and execution
sequence; default-RGB non-portability confirmed across the three tested paths;
mechanism, rate, generality, and intended colorimetry unresolved

**Evidence basis.** prospectively fixed factorial; exact archive, manifest,
identity, and result recomputation; unchanged target-runtime verifier after a
synthetic canary; independent execution and scientific reviews; and
independent decoder runs on three platform/build paths

**Evidence and trace.**

  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/oscar-input-reconstruction/protocol-oscar-repeatability-factorial.md`.
- Canonical summary and review:
  `result-oscar-repeatability-factorial.json` and
  `review-oscar-repeatability-factorial.md`.

### EXT-162 — Exchangeably weighted bootstrap theory is regularity-conditional and does not license boundary inference

**Finding.** Præstgaard and Wellner (1993) give sufficient conditions under
which exchangeably weighted empirical-process bootstraps satisfy central-limit
results. Cheng and Huang (2010) establish bootstrap consistency and
asymptotically correct confidence-set coverage for a broad class of
semiparametric M-estimators, including exchangeably weighted bootstraps, under
their stated regularity conditions. Andrews (2000) gives a counterexample in
which the bootstrap is inconsistent when the parameter is on the boundary.

Together these sources support using positive exchangeable multiplier weights
for regular, smooth M-estimation; they do not prove the E2 Davidson/Thurstone
maximum-statistic construction, finite-sample coverage, or inference at an
active Thurstone tie-parameter boundary. The E2 amendment therefore retains
all numerically qualified, support-preserving finite multiplier refits but
keeps a near-separated point estimate and an active point tie-parameter
constraint fail-closed. Simulation coverage and a separate boundary-valid
derivation remain required.

**Status.** source-confirmed as a general theory and boundary-warning scope;
E2-specific asymptotic and finite-sample validity unresolved

**Evidence basis.** primary publication records and article abstracts,
combined with the independently challenged E2 multiplier-gate diagnosis

**Evidence and trace.**

- Jens Præstgaard and Jon A. Wellner, “Exchangeably Weighted Bootstraps of the
  General Empirical Process,” *The Annals of Probability* 21(4), 2053–2086
  (1993), DOI `10.1214/aop/1176989011`, retrieved 2026-07-25.
- Guang Cheng and Jianhua Z. Huang, “Bootstrap Consistency for General
  Semiparametric M-Estimation,” *The Annals of Statistics* 38(5), 2884–2915
  (2010), DOI `10.1214/10-AOS809`; primary manuscript record
  `https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.1310`, retrieved 2026-07-25.
- Donald W. K. Andrews, “Inconsistency of the Bootstrap when a Parameter is on
  the Boundary of the Parameter Space,” *Econometrica* 68(2), 399–405 (2000),
  DOI `10.1111/1468-0262.00114`, retrieved 2026-07-25.
- E2 application and adjudication:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/prospective-study-design/review-e2-common-grid-protocol-independent-challenge.md`.

**Uncertainty and remaining validation.** The E2 estimator is a finite-
dimensional weighted likelihood, but its selected-set maximum statistic is
nonregular at ties and its exact assumptions are not established by these
general sources. Activation must empirically validate coverage across the
fixed boundary and misspecification scenarios; active point-boundary
inference requires a separate derivation or a different valid procedure.

**Status history.**

- 2026-07-25 — Created as `source-confirmed as a general theory and
  boundary-warning scope; E2-specific asymptotic and finite-sample validity
  unresolved` after primary-source verification and independent mathematical
  challenge of the E2 point/refit distinction.

### EXT-163 — Held-out sim-to-real validation is meaningful but does not identify a future-policy population

**Finding.** In the frozen 26-paper sim-to-real roster, the original
`supported` coding rule was not an exhaustive inferential assessment: it
required a target population or sampling mechanism plus axis-appropriate
uncertainty and therefore collapsed meaningful fixed-benchmark and held-out
predictive evidence into the same negative category as unvalidated displays.
A broadened source-only recoding identifies held-out predictive links in
multiple papers, including direct examples in RoboWorld, PolaRiS, SC3-Eval,
and Gemini/Veo. None of the 26 defines a probability distribution or sampling
frame over future policies/tasks together with calibrated population-level
predictive uncertainty. The defensible boundary is therefore bounded
benchmark/predictive validity under similarity or transport assumptions—not
“mere description,” and not formally identified population prediction.

**Status.** confirmed for the pinned 26-paper roster and stated five-category
schema

**Evidence basis.** source-verified; independently recoded

**Evidence and trace.**

- Full paper-level source review:

  and `audit_inference_links.py`.

  RoboWorld v4 Introduction/§5.3 (DROID training and held-out RoboArena
  evaluation), PolaRiS v2 §5.2 (15 held-out co-training environments and
  unseen target environments), SC3-Eval v3 Abstract/§3.3/§4.4 (task semantic
  absent from training and explicitly uncalibrated reliability signal), and

  OOD axes).
- Independent challenge and verified dispositions:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/claim-evidence-synthesis/review-hostile-validation-2026-07-26.md`.

**Uncertainty and remaining validation.** The five-category coding is
post-outcome and judgment-bearing. It should not be used for prevalence
estimation, and formal population prediction could be established by a later
source version or evidence outside the pinned reports. Random scenes,
trajectories, or episode initializations within some studies do not by
themselves probability-sample future policies or tasks.

### EXT-166 — Sparse pairwise top-k inference is more occupied than the P2 box result alone suggested

**Finding.** Two primary-source checks further narrow P2's novelty boundary.
Heckel et al. (2018) already study approximate subset/top-\(k\) selection using
average pairwise-win scores and explicitly discuss coupling constraints on
those scores. Li, Simchi-Levi, and Sun (2026) already combine sparse,
imbalanced pairwise data with low-rank BTL-type structure, debiased contrasts,
and simultaneous rank/top-\(K\) inference. P2 therefore cannot claim aggregate
pairwise-win values, pairwise coupling, structured sparse borrowing,
simultaneous sparse top-\(K\) inference, or approximate subset selection as
new.

The remaining candidate delta is narrower: assumption-light partial
identification under unsupported edges, projection to the worst real regret of
an independently evaluator-selected retained set, and honest behavior under
nontransitivity, clustering, random support, and missingness. This is a
novelty-risk boundary, not a proven absence claim.

**Status.** confirmed as a collision/boundary finding; P2 novelty remains
conditional.

**Evidence basis.** primary papers; bounded non-systematic collision search.

**Evidence and trace.**

- Heckel, Shah, Ramchandran, and Wainwright, *Approximate Ranking from Pairwise
  Comparisons*, AISTATS 2018:
  <https://proceedings.mlr.press/v84/heckel18a.html>.
- Li, Simchi-Levi, and Sun, *Low Rank for Rank: Uncertainty-Aware Task-Specific
  LLM Ranking under Sparse Pairwise Comparisons*, arXiv:2605.29395:
  <https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29395>.
- Local collision disposition:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/prospective-study-design/review-literature-collision.md`.

**Uncertainty and remaining validation.** The search is not systematic and
does not establish novelty by absence. Heckel et al. use an active ranking
problem and Li et al. impose structured BTL-type assumptions, whereas P2's
current box target is nonparametric and externally selects the retained set.
A submission-grade review must compare formal targets, assumptions, and
guarantees against these and the already recorded winner/multiple-winner and
sparse-ranking baselines.

**Status history.**

- 2026-07-26 — Added after primary full-text/abstract checks tightened the
  methods-paper contribution gate.

### EXT-167 — P3 calibration agreement must be class-specific and context-bounded

**Finding.** Primary measurement sources distinguish exact agreement from
chance-adjusted reliability and emphasize that agreement/reliability estimates
depend on the raters, objects, instrument, administration, and analysis
context. For binary coding, de Vet et al. specifically support reporting
positive- and negative-specific agreement rather than relying on Cohen's
kappa. Gwet's AC1 is an available chance-adjusted sensitivity coefficient, not
a substitute for raw or class-specific agreement. These findings changed the
P3 redesign: binary positive/negative agreement, reference sensitivity and
specificity, complete confusion matrices, and evidence-condition matching are
primary; kappa/AC1 are secondary only; and enriched-panel results cannot be
transported to the sealed candidate frame.

**Status.** confirmed as a methodological basis; P3 thresholds and construct
remain design choices requiring independent validation

**Evidence basis.** primary methodological papers and reporting guideline;
independent measurement-review prompt followed by primary-source verification

**Evidence and trace.**

- Kottner et al. (2011), GRRAS, DOI
  `10.1016/j.jclinepi.2010.03.002`.
- de Vet et al. (2013), *Clinicians are right not to like Cohen's kappa*, DOI
  `10.1136/bmj.f2125`.
- Gwet (2008), *Computing inter-rater reliability and its variance in the
  presence of high agreement*, DOI `10.1348/000711006X126600`.
- Local source and reliance record:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/evaluation-access-tax/review-p3-measurement-basis.md`.
- Revised design:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/evaluation-access-tax/protocol-p3-instrument-redesign.md`.

**Uncertainty and remaining validation.** These sources do not determine
P3's 0.80/0.90 thresholds, source composition, construct, or external
transport. The fixed enriched panel can qualify a coder pair only. Actual
candidate-frame double coding and category-specific uncertainty remain
necessary before any publication-grade reliability claim.

**Status history.**

- 2026-07-26 — Added after independent measurement challenge exposed the
  prevalence problem in overall agreement and primary-source checks confirmed
  the class-specific reporting basis.

### EXT-168 — The post-OSCAR RoboArena fixed-policy graph covers only 3 of 21 pair types

**Finding.** At pinned public RoboArena revision
`7931db81f3f6a48a3245427f7213a4c461f92ccc`, 33 sessions completed on or after
2026-06-16 contain at least two of the seven fixed OSCAR policies. Each of
those sessions contains exactly two fixed policies, for 66 records. They cover
only three pair types: policy-index pairs `(1,4)` in 9 sessions, `(1,6)` in
12, and `(4,6)` in 12. Eighteen of 21 pair types are absent.

Under P2's explicitly limited uniform-weight, all-policy-retained,
known-neutral-supported-edge box model, the missing degrees are
`[6,4,6,6,4,6,4]`. The sharp support penalty is therefore
\(12/(2\cdot7)=6/7\). For a 0.05 or 0.10 whole-panel tolerance, every one of
the 18 missing pair types is necessary before sampling uncertainty is
considered, because either tolerance is below the \(1/7\) penalty from even
one residual missing edge.

The same producer audit finds 2,798 multi-policy sessions and 8,617 records
before the cutoff, cumulatively covering all 21 pair types. Monthly topology
is unstable: July 2025 through January 2026 covers all 21 pairs,
February--April 2026 covers 15, and May--July 2026 covers three. The
February--April six-edge loss is entirely incident to policy 0. May has only
three sessions and its three edges form a matching, while June/July's three
edges form a triangle; several calendar windows are partial or tiny. The
triangle appears before and after the OSCAR cutoff, so the data do not support
a simple post-release onset and identify no cause. An independent narrow-field
re-extraction matched all monthly and cumulative counts.

**Status.** confirmed finite-release graph, temporal topology, and conditional
mathematical diagnostic; not a causal, common-estimand, transport, outcome,
or trial-sufficiency claim

**Evidence basis.** pinned public metadata; deterministic aggregate
calculation; independent timestamp/policy-name-only re-extraction and
mathematical challenge

**Evidence and trace.**

- Public source: `RoboArena/DataDump_07-17-2026`, revision
  `7931db81f3f6a48a3245427f7213a4c461f92ccc`.
- Canonical aggregate:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/prospective-study-design/result-historical-pair-support.json`.
- Producing code and internal checks:
  `analyze_historical_pair_support.py` and
  `test_analyze_historical_pair_support.py` in the same family.
- Proof and scope:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/prospective-study-design/proof-p2-sparse-screening.md`.
- Independent challenge:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/prospective-study-design/review-p2-historical-support.md`.

**Uncertainty and remaining validation.** Same-session co-occurrence is only
pair-type support; it does not establish a common task, site, evaluator, or
instruction estimand. The source YAML files contain outcomes and were parsed
in full, although no outcome field was referenced or used. The incidence hash
is a pseudonymous commitment derived from public session IDs. The graph is
disconnected with four isolated policies, so structured ranking methods also
lack an all-seven comparison path. Adding a pair type does not prescribe
repeat counts or remove sampling uncertainty. A paper-level result still needs
a decision-relevant retained set/target mixture, a more informative compatible
graph, or a broader multi-release feasibility study. Complete cumulative
historical support removes only the pooled graph's topology floor; a valid
historical target still needs common task/site/evaluator definitions,
standardization, clustering, and outcomes. It does not establish temporal
transport. Sparse recent support does not prove outcome drift or old-data
invalidity.

**Status history.**

- 2026-07-26 — Expanded after independent re-extraction matched all monthly
  pair counts and narrowed the interpretation to descriptive roster topology.
- 2026-07-26 — Added after independent re-extraction reproduced all 21 pair

### EXT-175 — The 2026 RoboArena policy-0 absence is incompatible with an exposed stable-assignment reference

**Finding.** In the pinned July 2026 RoboArena release, the exact two-policy
sessions from July 2025 through January 2026 contain policy 0 in 387 of 1,921
sessions, an empirical incidence of 0.20146. Policy 0 then occurs in 0 of 244
comparable two-policy sessions from February through April 2026, although the
other six fixed policies form a complete 15-edge graph in every one of those
three months. Under a hypothetical independent, exchangeable continuation of
the earlier empirical policy-0 incidence, the later expected count is 49.16
and the plug-in probability of observing zero is
\(1.45\times10^{-24}\). Across all 294 February--July two-policy sessions,
the expected count is 59.23 and the corresponding plug-in zero probability is
\(1.89\times10^{-29}\).

This is evidence against that declared stable empirical reference, not
identification of RoboArena's native assignment law. Its bounded decision
consequence is that a future-release intake must establish the active policy
roster and assignment epoch, or an explicit temporal bridge, before cumulative
historical pair coverage is used to support a current fixed-seven-policy
decision.

**Status.** provisional

### EXT-177 — WEAVER's reported offline policy evaluation requires the corresponding physical action trajectory

**Finding.** WEAVER's pinned paper states that its policy-evaluation path takes
recorded action trajectories from real-world rollouts and executes them
open-loop inside the world model. The same paper motivates this path as
offline policy evaluation that can reduce the need for costly real-world
rollouts. The authors' official project page and public implementation agree:
evaluation starts from a saved trajectory and conditions generated frames on
its recorded actions, or on action increments reconstructed from successive
recorded physical states.

This is a claim-specific temporal mismatch. The path can measure world-model
fidelity on already executed trajectories and may reduce additional labeling,
scoring, or repeated execution. It cannot by itself screen a not-yet-executed
policy or establish savings of the corresponding physical rollout, because
that rollout supplies a load-bearing input.

The finding does not apply to WEAVER's separate policy-improvement and
test-time-planning paths, which generate candidate actions inside the
world-model loop.

**Status.** independently source- and implementation-challenged within the
narrow corresponding-trace proposition

**Evidence basis.** pinned primary paper, authors' official project page, and
authors' public code at a pinned commit

**Evidence and trace.**

  Robotic Manipulation*, `arXiv:2606.13672v2`, Sections 3 and 5.2.1,

  <https://arnavkj1995.github.io/WEAVER/>.

  `3e41e90738fea9a7b142db6b2fd3d9ae72b7a82e`,
  <https://github.com/arnavkj1995/WEAVER>.

  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/evaluation-access-tax/review-weaver-action-provenance.md`.

### EXT-179 — Perfect same-execution replay does not identify unsupported policy value

**Finding.** Consider two deterministic one-step policies selecting actions
0 and 1. Let each action's reward be Bernoulli with mean in
\(\{0,1/2,1\}\). A corresponding physical execution of action \(j\) reveals
its complete Bernoulli law, and a best-case perfect replay returns its exact
mean.

Across all nine environments and both possible acquired actions, the six
observational-equivalence classes are defined by the acquired action and its
complete reward law. None identifies the best-policy set. In each of the two
classes with observed mean \(1/2\), setting the unsupported action mean to
either 0 or 1 preserves the observed law and perfect replay score while
reversing the unique best policy.

Separately, under an interface requiring one distinct corresponding physical-
execution trajectory before each candidate can be scored, scoring a
seven-candidate panel requires at least seven corresponding candidate
executions. This conditional set-cardinality statement does not rule out valid
historical reuse, overlap-based off-policy evaluation, structural or transport
assumptions, reductions in repeats or labels, or genuinely pre-execution
closed-loop evaluation.

**Status.** independently reproduced exact finite oracle

**Evidence basis.** exhaustive enumeration of the complete declared finite
class, analytic strict-reversal witnesses, policy-relabeling check, and five
known-answer tests

**Theory and novelty boundary.** This is a robotics-specific illustration of
the established overlap/support problem in off-policy evaluation, not a novel
general identification theorem. Khan, Saveski, and Ugander explicitly treat
no-overlap OPE as partial identification requiring added smoothness
assumptions. Thomas and Brunskill and Jiang and Li study policy evaluation
from data generated by another policy under the corresponding OPE framework.

**Evidence and trace.**

- Protocol and proof boundary:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/evaluation-access-tax/protocol-same-execution-replay-identification.md`.
- Exact implementation:
  `same_execution_replay_identification.py` in the same family.
- Canonical output:
  `result-same-execution-replay-identification.json` in the same family,
  SHA-256
  `427cb18e40c1d9a5ad34fcc9cfd8d3e747ff6ae50c99d708cf5092281e57bcca`.
- No-overlap partial identification:
  <https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11812>.
- Off-policy evaluation:
  <https://proceedings.mlr.press/v48/thomasa16> and
  <https://proceedings.mlr.press/v48/jiang16.html>.

**Uncertainty and remaining validation.** The one-step finite class isolates
support failure but omits sequential feedback, state shift, stochastic
policies, model error, and transport. The acquisition count is true only
under its declared interface. The result does not show that open-loop replay
is invalid for fidelity measurement, that OSCAR or WEAVER is inaccurate, or
that no legitimate savings are possible. The independent challenge verifies
the finite equivalence-class argument and conditional interface statement, not
sequential dynamics, transport, or broader cost claims.

**Status history.**

- 2026-07-27 — Added after the exact finite oracle, analytic witnesses,
  relabeling check, source-collision review, and five producer tests passed.
- 2026-07-27 — An independent Node implementation reproduced every finite
  count, both reversals, and relabeling invariance; separate analytic review
  confirmed the witness and conditional acquisition boundary. See
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/evaluation-access-tax/review-action-provenance-and-replay-independent-challenge.md`.

### EXT-180 — Systematic RoboArena A/B metadata-slot imbalance is not supported

**Finding.** In the exact July 17, 2026 RoboArena release, 2,219 of 3,883
metadata rows are A/B-only sessions containing two distinct members of the
fixed seven-policy roster. The lower-roster-index policy occupies metadata

### EXT-289 — PhAIL is public at its declared endpoint but full-release common support fails

**Finding.** The earlier PhAIL `NoSuchBucket` result was caused by querying
Amazon rather than the source-declared Nebius S3-compatible endpoint. Two
independent complete enumerations at
`https://storage.eu-north1.nebius.cloud` find 14,361 objects and
40,659,686,177 bytes under the official `phail/v1.0/dataset/` prefix. The
named cohort contains 594 paired rollout sidecars. The 524 episode IDs under
the newer `datasets/phail/v1.0/inference/` prefix are an exact
production-filtered subset. Both training prefixes contain 449 episode
identities; repository history changes the paper count from 352 to 449, and no
separate 352-episode manifest was found.

An outcome-blind audit of all 594 release sidecar pairs retains only episode,
policy/checkpoint, declared sampler context, creation time, public path, and
content-hash fields. The four policies appear in 17 of 19 full-window
`task × object × tote × camera` cells. After crossing the prospectively fixed
UTC date, only 18 of 126 observed cells contain all four policies. The
outcome-free restricted target retains 194 episodes and excludes 400.

This identifies a narrow positivity subset under the fixed UTC partition but
does not pass the release as a whole. Policy exposure is visibly batched: only
5 of 13 dates contain all four policies, 232 of 593 adjacent episodes repeat a
policy, and the longest run is 16. No source-established linked session
identifier was found; the traced server-recording locator is omitted from
episode metadata, and the fixed release inventory contains zero `.rrd` object
paths. Initial item count does not alter the subset. Chronology, carryover,
and effective sample adequacy remain unresolved, so performance outcomes
remain sealed.

A separately pinned post-`v0.2.1` source comparison does not change those
release facts. At public Positronic commit `01b78e6...070524`, all four current
PhAIL server commands still configure recording, and current code now writes
the configured server `.rrd` path to finalized episode `static.json` as
`inference.policy.server.recording.rrd`. The dataset writer separately records
a `uuid.uuid4().hex` episode `uid` in `meta.json`. The UUID is not a shared
server-session ID; the locator supplies the join and is not proven unique
across process restarts.

A fixed current release-surface audit at
`2026-07-28T10:32:17Z`--`10:32:19Z` finds that the complete, nontruncated
source-declared `phail/` storage listing contains only `phail/v1.0/`. The
official `v1.0` page responds, but `/releases` and `/sitemap.xml` both return
404. No fixed surface exposes a post-`v1.0` version. Because the site has no
usable index, this is `release_surface_incomplete`, not proof that no
unlinked site-only release exists and not an estimate of release frequency.

An exact pinned-current command trace then separates home mechanics from
physical-lifecycle evidence. The attended `phail` path binds the real DROID
arm/gripper home command, episode UUID, fixed UI context, and
server-recording join, but no `Task` scene reset, Harness-side pre-open
accepted-state gate, complete camera boundary, operator-session identity, or
persistent reset/carryover evidence.

A fixed endpoint comparison exposes a concrete historical-and-current
mechanism. Both Positronic `v0.2.1` and pinned current source bind the same
independent-uniform Franka home-joint perturbation, with half-widths
`[0.03, 0.05, 0.08, 0.08, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10]` radians. Its maximum possible
Euclidean joint-space norm is `0.2149418526020468` radians and RMS norm is
`0.12409673645990857` radians. Neither fixed source boundary serializes the
realized target or RNG identity.

A new fixed key-only census of all 1,188 hash-bound v1.0 sidecars finds three
apparent candidates in every episode: `joint_names`, `joint_signal`, and
`pose_signals`. Values remain unopened. Complete pinned source semantics show
that these fields are URDF joint-name and visualization signal-name
descriptors, not the configured or realized home target and not RNG evidence.
Independent implementations reproduce the endpoint mechanism, sidecar-key
census, and source-semantic null.

H218--H221 then test the assignment claim directly without opening outcomes.
Conditional on the complete released order and the four source-declared
context fields, the continuous zero-initialized
`BalancedSampler(balance=2)` reconstruction has log likelihood ratio
`BalancedSampler / uniform = -30.143563...`, or LR `8.1062e-14`.
Uniform assigns about `1.2336e13` times greater likelihood to the exact
594-policy sequence than that fixed balancing reconstruction. Resetting
sampler counts at either of the two pre-existing H206 clock regimes gives log
LR `-133.3770`; resetting by the 13 pre-existing UTC dates gives `-65.9720`.
Both coarse repairs also favor uniform. The complete context decomposition
has 12 of 19 groups favoring uniform, five favoring balancing, and two ties.
Independent Node.js/BigInt and Ruby/Rational implementations reproduce every
exact ratio, classification, and step-projection hash.

This is an outcome-free relative simple-model discrepancy, not proof of
uniform historical assignment, outcome-dependent assignment, or any
mechanism. Missing counted episodes, multiple output states, private
configuration, lifecycle events, creation-order mismatch, and publication
selection remain possible. It establishes that source code plus aggregate
balance does not reconstruct the historical unit propensities from the
released record.

**Status.** independently challenged bounded result; full-release and
chronology gates fail; restricted target identified; no performance claim

**Evidence basis.** source-declared endpoint and pinned release tooling;
independent complete inventory implementation; exact 594-episode
outcome-stripped manifest; per-sidecar SHA-256 hashes; exact contingency and
chronology calculations; rejected pre-reliance candidates; independently
recomputed final result

**Uncertainty and remaining validation.** The restricted 18-cell target was
selected only from outcome-free support, but it covers 194/594 episodes and
has not passed a chronology or exchangeability gate. H189 independently shows
that pre-assignment item count is deterministic within every dated H187 cell
and leaves the target unchanged. H191 exhausts 684 deterministic
width-by-phase calendar partitions: 24-hour phases retain 154--194 episodes in
15--19 supported cells, and H187's UTC cells each have minimum per-policy count
only one or two. The subset is therefore partition-dependent and thin, not a
source-recorded session target. H190 also finds no fixed-token session-artifact
path in the target rollout subtree or release root, but differently named or
internally stored fields remain possible. H193 follows the differently named
route with an independently reproduced key-only census of all 1,188
hash-bound sidecars. It finds `server.host` in 594 episodes and
`server.device` in 267. H194's result-exposed exhaustive value/source census
then shows that host is the constant server bind address `0.0.0.0`, while
device is the generic accelerator label `cuda` for ACT/SmolVLA and missing for
GR00T/OpenPI. Pinned Positronic source semantics and independent challenge
show that neither field supplies execution-instance, physical-device, session,
or dependence-cluster identity. These bounded results do not resolve
chronology. H195 traces a materially different source path and finds that all
four public PhAIL server configurations activate `RecordingCodec`. Each
server policy reset creates a session-specific `.rrd` locator from
second-resolution time plus a process-local counter, but the metadata wrapper
does not expose it to the ready handshake or episode writer. The complete
fixed public release inventory has zero `.rrd` paths. This does not establish
cross-restart uniqueness or that configured server recording locations are
unavailable or empty; the locator is not a physical reset, operator session,
or dependence cluster.
H196 independently reconstructs the later pinned endpoint and finds a
two-field repair: a UUID episode identity plus the server-recording locator in
episode static metadata. This current-code result does not establish the code
used for the historical PhAIL evaluation, retroactively modify the public
release, provide a single shared end-to-end session ID, or resolve chronology.
H197 finds only `v1.0` on the complete source-declared storage-version
surface at one retrieval time. The site-wide result remains incomplete because
the expected release index and sitemap return 404. The current implementation
repair is therefore not demonstrated in a post-`v1.0` public release.
H198--H202 further show source-bound home mechanics and an unrecorded
randomized target, while closing three public sidecar key candidates as
generic schema descriptors without opening their values. H202 then
prospectively opens only the first exact joint-state/error pair and
independently reconstructs a nonerror achieved first arm state for all 594
episodes. Its spread matches the configured randomized-home scale, but it is
an achieved observation rather than the commanded draw. This does not
establish that the historical release executed the tagged source exactly,
recover RNG identity, prove reset acceptance, establish complete physical
context, show that randomization was harmful, imply that episodes are
dependent or nonexchangeable, or show that performance changed.
H203's prospectively fixed global, within-policy, and within-UTC-date
successive-distance tests detect no material temporal structure at their
fixed 0.01 threshold; an independent Node permutation implementation agrees.
This blocks a positive clustering claim at that resolution but does not prove
independence, authenticate physical execution order, exclude carryover, or
establish valid outcome uncertainty units.
H204 further finds no material policy mean association conditional on UTC
date (partial variance share 0.00392, p=0.777) and no material date mean
association conditional on policy (0.01760, p=0.811). An independent
SciPy/Philox reconstruction agrees. This supports only achieved seven-joint
mean balance at the fixed resolution, not randomized assignment, full
physical balance, exchangeability, or outcome validity.
H205 further finds no material marginal-uniformity departure (maximum KS
0.04071, p=0.891) or cross-joint-dependence departure (maximum absolute
correlation 0.13117, p=0.0282; both fixed material gates unmet). A separate
SciPy/Philox reconstruction agrees within `2.78e-17`. Ten achieved joint
values exceed nominal support only slightly, with maximum normalized
exceedance 0.01139. This supports only achieved-state consistency with the
simple reference at fixed resolution, not commanded-draw or RNG validity,
reset acceptance, historical execution fidelity, full physical balance, or
proof of independence.
H206 then exposes a partial chronology repair. Pinned source defines the
retained primary trajectory timestamp as `time.monotonic_ns()` and episode
creation as `time.time_ns()`. Their difference yields two scale-separated
clock-offset regimes of 250 and 344 episodes: the largest adjacent gap is
1,556,979.985 seconds, 3.06 million times the next-largest gap. Within both
regimes, wall-clock and monotonic order have zero discordant pairs, and offset
spans are only 72.2 ms and 936.8 ms across multi-day collection windows. An
independent Node/BigInt implementation reproduces all 594 projection rows
byte-for-byte. H206 is explicitly result-exposed exploratory evidence; it
source-qualifies within-regime chronology but does not identify a host,
reboot, operator session, physical reset, carryover unit, exchangeability
cluster, or valid uncertainty unit.
H207 fixes the direct follow-up before computing any achieved-state distance
inside those regimes. Restricting H203's adjacency and permutations to the
250/344 partition gives a pooled observed/permutation-median ratio of 1.03060
with two-sided p=0.04984 against the fixed p<=0.01 and 10% material gate.
Regime-specific ratios are 1.02690 (p=0.26804) and 1.03346 (p=0.10196);
neither passes its fixed p<=0.005 gate. An independent Node/SplitMix64
implementation reproduces the observed statistics within `7.1e-14` and the
same bounded-null classification. H207 closes this positive temporal-
structure branch at the tested resolution; it does not establish
independence, physical order, sessions, carryover absence, or valid
uncertainty units.
H208 then distinguishes chronology from an estimable regime effect. All 13
UTC dates map to exactly one regime, and the regime-2 indicator is exactly the
sum of six date indicators; adding regime to the saturated date design leaves
rank unchanged at 13. All eight policy-regime cells are observed (18--146
episodes), but empirical policy composition differs with total-variation
distance 0.38572 and descriptive Cramer's V 0.45154. An independent
Ruby/Rational reconstruction agrees exactly. H208 therefore blocks a
separately identified date-adjusted regime effect on this release while
showing coarse structural policy overlap. It does not establish randomization,
precision, exchangeability, session identity, causality, or outcome validity.
H209 then tests ordered policy labels without opening state or outcomes.
Pooled same-policy adjacency is 0.39189 versus permutation median 0.30574
(p=0.00004), but its 0.08615 excess misses the fixed 0.10 pooled material
gate. Regime 1 supplies the fixed secondary signal: 0.48594 versus 0.32129,
an excess of 0.16466 (p=0.00004). Regime 2 does not (p=0.23864). An
independent Node/SplitMix64 implementation agrees. This supports a bounded
assignment/block metadata request, not a material pooled batching claim,
assignment law, scheduler/session identity, outcome dependence, or
performance effect.
H210 then conditions the same diagnostic on every UTC date. Pooled
same-policy adjacency is 0.39243 versus permutation median 0.38038, an excess
of 0.01205 (p=0.52872). The regime-1-date excess is 0.03704 (p=0.23688) and
the regime-2-date excess is -0.00296 (p=0.90884). An independent
Node/SplitMix64 implementation agrees on the fixed bounded-null
classification. H210 therefore narrows H209's signal to coarse date
composition or date boundaries at the tested resolution, but does not prove
that mechanism, identify assignment or scheduling, validate exchangeability,
or authorize outcomes.
H218--H219 then reject the simplest continuous source-law reconstruction
relative to uniform by an exact LR of `8.1062e-14`. H220--H221 show that
resetting at the complete two-regime or 13-date partitions does not repair
the relative signature and that 12/19 context groups favor uniform. This
sharpens the native assignment-ledger request but does not identify the
historical law, prove uniformity, or authorize performance analysis.
Public storage can change; rerun inventory and content hashes before release
reliance.

and a real public-data application, but not a global ranking result. The
release fails the exact full-window no-extrapolation gate in two singleton
cells; stronger time conditioning yields partition-sensitive, sparsely
supported subsets rather than an actionable target. Outcomes cannot advance
until session/chronology, exchangeability, and precision requirements are
resolved. The source trace now gives a concrete repair: propagate a
collision-resistant episode identity and the configured server-recording
locator into released episode metadata while separately recording physical
reset/carryover and operator-session identity. Pinned current code implements
the first two in split form; systems requiring one end-to-end identity should
also propagate a shared collision-resistant inference-session ID. H197 adds a
deployment/versioning requirement: publish a discoverable release index and
bind each scientific release to its exact storage prefix and writer revision.
H198--H202 add and refine a physical-lifecycle requirement: the release
already permits reconstruction of achieved first arm state, but should still
gate episode opening on a source-qualified accepted state and retain the
commanded/realized home target, RNG identity, scene/gripper state,
reset/carryover evidence, and operator-session identity when needed for
reproduction or dependence adjustment. This is an evidence request, not a
claim that the randomization or released performance is invalid.
H203 prevents strengthening that request with a positive temporal-clustering
claim from the released first arm states alone; the request remains based on
missing authenticated lifecycle and uncertainty-unit evidence.
H204--H205 likewise prevent strengthening it with a policy/date mean-imbalance
or achieved-state distributional-departure claim at their fixed resolutions.
They do not remove the underlying request for commanded target/RNG,
authenticated reset/carryover, complete physical context, or valid
uncertainty units.
H206 partially repairs chronology by source-qualifying order within two
clock-offset regimes. The remaining request should no longer imply that no
trajectory chronology is public; it should ask for explicit machine,
operator-session, reset/carryover, and dependence-unit identities joined to
that chronology. H207 prevents strengthening that request with a positive
within-regime temporal-structure claim at the fixed resolution. H208 further
prevents treating the clock partition as a separately estimable date-adjusted
effect, while retaining only coarse policy-regime structural overlap.
H209 adds a bounded label-scheduling reason to request native assignment and
block metadata, without converting that request into an outcome-dependence or
performance claim.
H210 prevents strengthening that request into a finer within-day scheduling
claim at the fixed resolution. The request should focus on explicit native
assignment/block metadata rather than further post hoc timestamp
subpartitioning; the protocol closes individual-date, sub-day, transition,
and run-level refinement.
H218--H221 make that request load-bearing: publish sampler
implementation/configuration identity, pre-draw state or sufficient counts,
exact unit probabilities, random-draw identity, completion/count updates,
retry/cancellation status, and process/output-state identity in an append-only
assignment lifecycle. Do not infer those fields from aggregate balance or the
public source alone.

### EXT-295 — FeelWorld is pre-action world-model planning, not a frozen policy evaluator

**Finding.** FeelWorld (`arXiv:2607.24267v1`) genuinely uses a learned
visuo-tactile world model before physical actions: at each control cycle it
scores imagined candidate action sequences, executes the first two actions
from the selected sequence on a real Imeta-Y1 robot, observes the resulting
state, and replans. This is an online closed-loop action selector, not a
post-execution video scorer.

It does not instantiate H022's frozen evaluator over immutable policy
checkpoints. The paper compares three planner variants rather than a
versioned active policy/checkpoint roster; states a 50-step horizon and 40
real-robot trials per task but does not define the success predicate or
evaluator identity in the fixed paper scope; and supplies no assignment/order
law, trial/session dependence identity, missingness rule, dependence-aware
uncertainty method, immutable evaluated-checkpoint manifest, or public
per-trial ledger.

It also does not add a P1 paired case. Prediction-quality and real-planning
tables share some method families, but the source provides no exact
common-unit join and makes no association, rank-agreement, selection, or
predictive-validity claim between a pre-execution model score and standalone
real-policy outcomes. Constructing a correlation across the three visible
method correspondences would be an outcome-exposed audit-authored analysis
with mismatched aggregation, not recovery of a source claim. That lower-value
branch was not opened.

**Status.** independently challenged negative intake for H022 and P1; no
separate hypothesis opened

**Evidence basis.** exact official v1 PDF/source identities; source-located
ten-unit design audit; five visually checked PDF pages; independent Node
decision reconstruction

**Evidence and trace.**

- fixed protocol:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/decision-validity/protocol-h225-feelworld-paper-intake.md`;
- official PDF: 2,056,855 bytes, SHA-256
  `e1f36f7189b8ff8a286427ba8741701711feee003ab1973f46895d2760fcffdd`;

  `3cdaddc194bb9de7269dd338c7efbaaeefa7245fc448dcdc17e1a89b5f8043d2`;

  `ff7c192e83ac1cf41f80a8fab8d4a10b5e8f0f213c447fd7c2b22f1a4d43e225`;

### EXT-296 — NEO validates predicted physical future scenes, but its advertised dataset is not publicly released

**Finding.** A prospectively fixed abstract triage of the three remaining
H222 arXiv papers advanced only NEO (`2607.24538v1`) to full-paper intake.
FloAff-Kitchen's abstract does not identify standalone physical execution or
a prediction/physical-outcome join. PAC-DP is a policy-training and
generalization method rather than a pre-execution evaluator joined to
physical outcomes. NEO explicitly predicts future scene state before robot
action and reports both editing-method comparisons and pick-and-place robot
experiments. Separate implementations agree on all 18 triage-axis statuses
and all three decisions.

NEO's official v1 paper confirms a genuine, non-circular
prediction-to-physical-reality design. An initial scan and desired object
transform produce an edited NeRF before physical execution. Fixed Franka
Panda and UR5 arms perform controlled object moves, and rendered predictions
are evaluated against registered real post-action scans. The paper describes
six manipulation scenes, two editing methods for the pick-and-place
comparison, and a four-step physical assembly sequence.

This result is scientifically distinct from the current paper chain. It is
not a P1 case because the physical target is post-manipulation scene
appearance/geometry rather than policy success, return, or selection. It is
not H022 because NEO is not a frozen evaluator over immutable policy
checkpoints. It is not a P2 design contrast because the central object is
scene-editing metrology rather than finite real-policy evaluation design. It
does identify a coherent adjacent question: validating pre-action world-model
predictions against registered physical future states.

That branch is not executable from the observed public release. The
author-linked project page describes twelve registered scenes, but its

### EXT-268 — Fixed-panel nonidentification floors do not transfer freely through evaluator selection

**Finding.** P2's fixed-retained-set honest-confidence floor cannot be
promoted to a data-dependent evaluator-selected set at the same confidence
level solely because coverage is uniform over fixed pair completions.

In the exact H142 construction, two uniformly weighted policies have one
completely unsupported half-win edge \(x\in[0,1]\). Both singleton retained
sets have fixed-set identification floor \(1/2\). Under a common
parameter-invariant observed-data law, one probability-\(\alpha\) event
selects policy 0 and reports upper bound zero, a disjoint
probability-\(\alpha\) event selects policy 1 and reports zero, and the
remaining event reports \(1/2\). For every fixed \(x\), at most one low-bound
selection event is a coverage failure, so coverage is at least
\(1-\alpha\). But the bound is below the identification floor of the realized
selected set on both disjoint events.

At \(\alpha=.05\), minimum fixed-completion coverage is exactly 0.95 while
selected-floor coverage is exactly 0.90. More generally, when the finite
selection range is \(\mathcal S\), each fixed-set floor is attained by a
completion with the same observed-data law, and \(U\) is uniformly honest,

\[
P^*\{U<B^*(\widehat S)\}\le|\mathcal S|\alpha.
\]

The two-set H142 construction attains equality. H143 independently reproduces
the result with Ruby exact rational arithmetic over 1,001 parameter values and
verifies the quantifier argument.

**Status.** confirmed exact finite counterexample and finite-selection union
statement; not a complete adaptive or cluster-valid confidence method

**Evidence basis.** analytic finite construction, exact rational known
answers, independent language/implementation reconstruction, and explicit
quantifier challenge

**Evidence and trace.**

- H142 protocol/result:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/prospective-study-design/protocol-h142-adaptive-selection-confidence-floor.md`
  and `result-h142-adaptive-selection-confidence-floor.json`, result SHA-256
  `dbf5021d4392a5d42ddc33a82e9569d3560257c88d1a6aec078124b80ceac1f4`.
- Independent H143:

- Reproduction:

  `make h143-adaptive-selection-floor-challenge`.

**Uncertainty and remaining validation.** The union result assumes a finite

selection-independent calibration, or a single full-object joint region can

clustering, adaptive support generation, informative missingness, or
continuous target adaptation.

### EXT-269 — Complete all-pair permutations yield a sharp, useful P2 joint region

**Finding.** For \(K\ge3\) policies and \(n={K\choose2}\) fixed contexts, let
one complete block uniformly permute all unordered pair labels over the
contexts. For any ordered uniform-reference policy-value contrast and
arbitrary fixed pair/context half-win potential outcomes in \([0,1]\), the
sharp worst-case randomization variance is

\[
V_K^\star
=\frac{2\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor}{K\,n(n-1)}.
\]

The proof double-centers the coefficient-weighted potential-outcome matrix.
Uniform-permutation variance is its squared Frobenius norm divided by
\(n-1\). Column-centering followed by row projection gives the upper bound;
a maximally balanced binary construction with constant coefficient-scaled
row sums attains it. H144 independently motivates the formula by exhausting
all 512 K=3 binary matrices and all six assignments, obtaining \(2/9\) with
six maximizers. H145 verifies exact attaining witnesses for K=3 through K=12.

At K=7 the sharp cap is \(11/147\), only \(11/108\) of the generic
range-squared-over-four cap \(36/49\). For eight equal target strata and
\(B\) mutually independent complete blocks per stratum, the averaged
contrast has deterministic Bernstein inputs

\[
V=\frac{11}{1176B},\qquad c=\frac{3}{14B}.
\]

An outward-certified 95% simultaneous band over all 42 ordered contrasts has
minimum \(B\) values 2, 23, 70, and 241 per stratum for radii 1, .10, .05,
and .025. The five-point design therefore uses 11,760 sessions. The same
complete-block design requires 86,352 sessions with generic-cap Bernstein
and 83,160 with block Hoeffding. On the one joint contrast event, projection
to worst regret covers all 127 nonempty evaluator-selected retained sets, so
it does not incur EXT-268's fixed-set union loss.

A pre-challenge semantic audit corrected the estimator description by
restoring the known stored-edge affine constant \((i-s)/7\). The constant
cancels from randomization errors, so no variance or width changed. H147
reconstructed the K=3 census, K=7 attaining witness, affine target, width
minima and predecessors, and all selected sets in Ruby without importing the
producer modules; it reported no critical disagreement.

**Status.** confirmed sharp variance theorem and positive cluster-valid
finite-context simultaneous region for complete independent uniform pair
permutations

**Evidence basis.** analytic permutation identity and projection proof,
exact rational exhaustive small-case computation, constructive sharpness,
outward-certified confidence calculations, deterministic selected-set
exhaustion, and independent-language reconstruction

**Evidence and trace.**

- H144 protocol/result:
  `sim2real-correlation-audit/research/prospective-study-design/protocol-h144-k3-pairwise-permutation-variance.md`
  and `result-h144-k3-pairwise-permutation-variance.json`, result SHA-256
  `12e35bf777b63c5e005f3835099bd6a8deba5ce62d9160b7b3c4815770b762b1`.
